title: Concepts in Marketing, Sales, and Customer Contact

questions.q: Which concept refers to the number of product versions in a product line?
questions.explanation: Depth = number of product versions within ONE product line. Width = number of different product lines a company has. Mix = total combination of all products.

questions.q: The marketing manager of a breakfast cereal issues coupons to encourage purchase. Which element of the marketing mix do the coupons represent?
questions.explanation: Coupons are sales promotion (per Lesson 2). Promotion includes advertising, sales promotion, PR, personal selling, social media, and digital marketing. Coupons influence the customer to buy = Promotion, NOT Price.

questions.q: What type of vertical marketing system is a franchise?
questions.explanation: Franchises are CONTRACTUAL VMS - the franchisor and franchisee are bound by a written contract. Corporate VMS = single company owns the whole channel. Administered VMS = informal coordination by a dominant member.

questions.q: A donut shop owner decides to use radio to advertise weekly specials. Which element of the marketing mix is the donut shop using?
questions.explanation: Radio advertising = communication with customers = Promotion. Note: the SPECIALS are price-related but the act of advertising via radio is a Promotion activity.

questions.q: At the end of a cosmetic tutorial video, the website marketer posts a special offer code for 20% off first purchases. Which element of the marketing mix does the special offer code represent?
questions.explanation: Discount codes posted in marketing content = sales promotion. Even though the code lowers the price paid, the activity (offering a code to drive purchase) is Promotion. Lesson 2: 'sales promotion' is one of the components of Promotion.

questions.q: What is an example of an uncontrollable element within the marketing planning process?
questions.explanation: Uncontrollable = external/macro environment (PESTLE). Regulations are political/legal forces companies cannot control. Price/Promotion/Redesign are CONTROLLABLE marketing mix decisions.

questions.q: A home improvement retail store offers 60 days of no interest for credit card purchases. Which element of the marketing mix is represented by this offer?
questions.explanation: Financing terms (no interest, payment plans, credit terms) = Price element. Price is everything related to what the customer pays, including TIME/TERMS of payment, not just the dollar amount.

questions.q: An electronics company invites industry employees to test the capabilities of its new low-cost digital multi-meters and provide design feedback. Which element of the marketing mix is represented?
questions.explanation: Soliciting design feedback during development = Product element. Product encompasses design, features, quality, and the development process itself.

questions.q: An assistant marketing manager is instructed to write the portion of the company's marketing plan that discusses the controllable elements of the marketing environment. Which element will the manager write about?
questions.explanation: Controllable = the 4Ps (Product, Price, Promotion, Place). Cultural, ecological, and technological are UNCONTROLLABLE macro forces. Only Promotional is part of the 4Ps.

questions.q: Which uncontrollable variables, such as inflation, unemployment, exchange rates, and consumer confidence, affect how a company markets its products in both domestic and global market conditions?
questions.explanation: Inflation, unemployment, exchange rates, consumer confidence = ECONOMIC factors. Political = laws/regulations. Social = culture/demographics. Environmental = ecological/natural.

questions.q: Which uncontrollable elements, such as shifts in values, attitudes, and the makeup of the workforce, influence marketers' decisions?
questions.explanation: Values, attitudes, demographics of the workforce = SOCIO-CULTURAL factors. These shape consumer preferences and how marketing messages are received.

questions.q: A woman visits a baby store, planning to buy a crib for $100. The salesperson tells her that the $100 crib is no longer available but a $250 crib can be purchased. The woman can see the $100 crib boxes on a shelf. Which pricing tactic was the salesperson attempting to use?
questions.explanation: BAIT AND SWITCH = advertise low-priced item to lure customer in, then claim it's unavailable and push them to a higher-priced item. Classic unethical tactic. Visible inventory makes it especially deceptive.

questions.q: What is an ethical marketing practice related to distribution?
questions.explanation: Distribution = Place. Ethical Place issues include fair labor in supply chain, sustainable logistics, fair channel partner relationships. The other 3 options are Promotion (a), Product (b), and Price (c) ethics.

questions.q: A programmer develops new software that is more effective at analyzing the stock market than any other software. The programmer plans to sell this software at a higher price until competitors catch up. Which pricing strategy is used?
questions.explanation: PRICE SKIMMING = launch new innovative product HIGH, lower the price as competitors catch up. Penetration = launch LOW to gain market share. Leader = price below cost as a loss leader. Bundle = group products.

questions.q: What does price determine for the company?
questions.explanation: Price is the ONLY element of the marketing mix that generates revenue (and therefore profit). The other 3 Ps (Product, Place, Promotion) all create costs. Value is what the CUSTOMER perceives, not what the company determines.

questions.q: What is the term for the income a company receives from the sale of goods or services?
questions.explanation: REVENUE = total income from sales (price × quantity). Profit = revenue minus costs. Sales = the act/quantity of goods sold. Market share = company's % of total industry sales.

questions.q: Which controllable element is included in the marketing mix?
questions.explanation: Marketing mix = 4 Ps: Product, Price, Place, Promotion. These are CONTROLLABLE by the company. Legal/Environmental/Political are uncontrollable macro forces.

questions.q: A marketing manager wants to increase revenue from existing products in the company's most profitable markets. The manager begins by evaluating opportunities for more retail partnerships. Which component of marketing planning is the manager using?
questions.explanation: SITUATIONAL ANALYSIS = examining controllable and uncontrollable elements that shape the current state. Evaluating retail partnership opportunities is analyzing the current environment - that's situational analysis.

questions.q: What is required for a marketing plan objective to be clear, quantifiable, and timely?
questions.explanation: SMART = Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound. The framework specifically for writing objectives. SWOT is environmental analysis. Porter's = industry competition. BCG = portfolio analysis.

questions.q: A marketing manager is performing a SWOT analysis. The manager notes that newly enacted laws will make it easier to sell the company's products in foreign countries. Where do these findings belong in a SWOT analysis framework?
questions.explanation: OPPORTUNITIES = EXTERNAL + POSITIVE. Laws are external. Easier to sell = positive. SWOT: S/W = internal, O/T = external. + = S/O, - = W/T.

questions.q: A marketing manager wants to focus the marketing department's efforts to achieve the best possible result. Which business component should the marketing manager create to accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation: OBJECTIVES focus efforts and define what success looks like. They give the team a clear target to work toward. Situational analysis is the input; objectives are the focus.

questions.q: A manager is considering the economics of an industry's factors that determine how competitive, attractive, and profitable the market is. Which planning tool is being used?
questions.explanation: PORTER'S FIVE FORCES = industry competitive analysis: competitive rivalry, supplier power, buyer power, threat of substitutes, threat of new entrants. SWOT is broader. BCG is portfolio. Pro forma is forecasting.

questions.q: A company analyzes its internal and external environments, identifies the needs of its target market, and develops a plan for accomplishing its mission, objectives, and goals. Which component of the marketing planning process has the company developed?
questions.explanation: MARKETING PLAN = the comprehensive document that ties together situational analysis, objectives, strategies, and tactics. Tactical planning is the HOW (specific actions). Implementation is doing. Performance analysis is reviewing results.

questions.q: What is the first step in the marketing planning process?
questions.explanation: Examining marketing opportunities (situational analysis) comes FIRST. You can't pick a target market or design a mix until you understand the environment and opportunities available.

questions.q: What are the 4Ps in the marketing mix?
questions.explanation: Memorize: Product, Price, Promotion, Place. People is in the EXTENDED 7Ps services framework but not in the classic 4Ps.

questions.q: Which is a likely consequence of new competitor entering a market with established players?
choices: Sales and profit potential for the industry as a whole will rise
Established players will invest more to maintain their market share
The bargaining power of buyers will decline
There will be less competition between current rivals
questions.explanation: New entrants = MORE competition. Established players defend by investing more in marketing/innovation/price. Buyer power INCREASES with more options. Profit per company DECREASES, not increases.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of market planning?
choices: To identify the company's marketing goals and ensure that they follow the organization's mission and vision
To understand a company's overall strategy to attract potential customers and convert them into buyers
To gather data so that a business is aware of both previous and present market trends
To assist businesses in comprehending the many demographic segments that comprise their market
questions.explanation: Marketing PLANNING is about defining marketing goals aligned with the company mission/vision. The other options describe parts of the process (research, segmentation) but not the main purpose.

questions.q: A salesperson pitches a new product to a customer in a face-to-face meeting. What aspect of marketing promotion does this example involve?
questions.explanation: Face-to-face sales pitch = textbook PERSONAL SELLING. E-commerce is online transactions. Content marketing creates educational/entertaining content. Influencer marketing uses third-party promoters.

questions.q: Which ethical guideline should marketers keep in mind when obtaining secondary data content?
questions.explanation: Secondary data = data already collected by others. The ethical concern is EVALUATING CREDIBILITY of the source. Consent/independent responses/understanding are issues with PRIMARY data collection (surveys, interviews).

questions.q: Which component of the marketing mix is related to logistics, channel management, and transportation?
questions.explanation: PLACE = distribution = logistics, channels, transportation, warehousing, retail location. Getting product to customer = Place.

questions.q: Which term covers all efforts related to creation of customer value and establishment of long-lasting customer relationships?
questions.explanation: MARKETING STRATEGY is the umbrella term for all efforts to create value and build customer relationships. Segmentation is one tactic. Marketing mix is the 4 Ps tools. Analysis is research.

questions.q: An air conditioning company wants to increase sales by offering their existing products to new geographical areas. Which growth strategy is this company using?
choices: Convincing current clients to buy more units
Gaining new customers in new segments
Identifying the needs of potential customers
questions.explanation: EXISTING product + NEW market = MARKET DEVELOPMENT (Ansoff matrix). 'New geographical areas' = new market segments. Option B is the description of market development. Options A and D are market penetration.

questions.q: An apparel company became the number-one provider in the U.S. New customers had switched to this company's clothing line instead of buying from competitors. Which strategic opportunity did the company use to achieve this goal?
questions.explanation: EXISTING product + EXISTING market + STEALING customers from competitors = MARKET PENETRATION. Same product, same market, just more share.

questions.q: A manager wants to determine whether existing RV customers would expand the use of their RVs as food trucks and would purchase a special food truck add-on package. The manager plans to create designs for the add-on package and test with current RV owners. Which growth strategy is being used?
questions.explanation: NEW product (food truck add-on) + EXISTING customers (current RV owners) = PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT. The Ansoff matrix: existing market + new product = product development.

questions.q: Which factor affects how companies develop strong relationships that lead to profit gains and high customer lifetime value?
questions.explanation: MARKETING ACTIVITIES drive customer relationships and CLV. Ongoing engagement, loyalty programs, communications - all marketing activities - build the relationships that yield long-term profit.

questions.q: Which equity driver involves assessing the uniqueness of a company's product from its competitors?
questions.explanation: BRAND EQUITY = how the customer assesses the value of the BRAND, above its objective value (i.e., the unique brand identity beyond product features). Value equity = the product/service value. Retention equity = stickiness.

questions.q: In organization A, details on contacts and touchpoints with leads, prospects and purchasers are stored in the computer system to improve services and for targeted marketing. Which type of information is this organization using?
questions.explanation: Information about leads/prospects/purchasers stored for CRM = CUSTOMER DATA. Government stats = census/economic data. Industry intelligence = competitor research. Shareholder research = financial.

questions.q: Advancements in technology have enabled an e-commerce website to deliver orders within 2 days. But at the same time, the company must monitor for hackers attempting to gain access to its customers' information. What challenge of CRM is involved?
questions.explanation: Hackers + customer information = DATA PRIVACY. Major CRM challenge: protecting the customer data the system stores. Required for trust and legal compliance.

questions.q: Which action includes selecting a segment to serve as the focus of the marketing team's efforts?
questions.explanation: TARGETING = selecting which segment(s) to focus on. STP = Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning. Niche is a TYPE of targeting strategy (concentrated). Differentiation is a positioning approach.

questions.q: A marketing manager wants to forecast what current customers might purchase in the future. Which variable should the marketing manager use?
questions.explanation: PAST PURCHASES are the strongest predictor of FUTURE purchases. Behavioral segmentation/predictive analytics fundamentally rests on this. Geography/lifestyle predict cohort behavior, not specific customer behavior.

questions.q: Which marketing approach is more prevalent in B2B transactions than in B2C?
questions.explanation: B2B = high-value, complex, relationship-driven sales = PERSONAL SELLING dominates. B2C = mass marketing/advertising/social media dominates. B2B sales cycles need consultative one-on-one approaches.

questions.q: What type of marketing is a company using if their efforts are directed towards a specific group?
questions.explanation: Specific group = TARGET marketing. Mass/undifferentiated = same message to everyone. Target = focused on a defined segment.

questions.q: Which factor is used more efficiently when a target market has been identified?
questions.explanation: Lesson 28: 'Concentrating on potential customers lets the firm use its resources efficiently.' Identifying a target market lets a company spend FISCAL RESOURCES (money) where they'll have the most impact.

questions.q: A mattress retailer offers graduated rebates to different customers based on the size and quality of the mattress purchased. Several commercials highlight each mattress with its accompanying rebate. What targeting strategy is being used?
questions.explanation: DIFFERENTIATED targeting = multiple segments, each with its OWN tailored marketing mix. Different rebates + different commercials for different mattress tiers = textbook differentiated. Concentrated = one segment. Undifferentiated = all segments same. Micro = individual.

questions.q: A marketing department is reviewing a new Super Bowl ad for the company with the goal to reach the largest possible audience. Which marketing approach is being used?
questions.explanation: Largest possible audience = MASS MARKETING (undifferentiated, same message to everyone). Super Bowl ads are the canonical example of mass marketing.

questions.q: An automotive manufacturer is ranked as the leading brand among competitors for cars costing over $75,000 and enjoys strong brand recognition in the market. Which form of positioning advantage does this company have?
questions.explanation: PRODUCT CATEGORY positioning = positioning within a recognized category (luxury cars). Per Lesson 31's exact example: 'BMW competes with other luxury vehicles in its category.' The $75K+ luxury category is the key signal. Product price would say 'lowest cost' or 'best value', not 'leading brand in $75K+ category.'

questions.q: In its ads and product literature, Phone A brand commonly compares its products and operating systems against Phone B and their operating systems. Which positioning strategy is being used by the Phone A brand?
questions.explanation: Direct comparison against a competitor = COMPETITION positioning. Lesson 31's exact example: 'Cell phone operating systems (Android versus iOS).'

questions.q: A hair shampoo communicates its use as a two products in one, a shampoo and a conditioner. The message is that consumer will save both time and money by using the one product. Which positioning strategy is being used?
questions.explanation: ATTRIBUTES positioning = highlighting product characteristics. Lesson 31's EXACT example: '2-in-1 shampoo and conditioner' is given as the canonical example of Product attributes positioning. Application would be 'best for occasion X.'

questions.q: A company is launching a new product. The marketing team will find the target customers by first segmenting the existing customers in the market. Which is NOT a common type of segmentation?
questions.explanation: The four MAIN segmentation types: Geographic, Demographic, Psychographic, Behavioral. Family size is a SUB-VARIABLE within demographic, not a top-level segmentation type.

questions.q: An individual bought a premium computer but is now concerned that it will be obsolete after a friend mentions a newer version coming out soon. The individual wishes the purchase had been delayed. Which form of dissonance is this?
questions.explanation: Already bought + now regretting = POST-PURCHASE dissonance (buyer's remorse). Pre-purchase would be hesitation BEFORE buying.

questions.q: A marketer decides to use a community spokesperson in an advertisement. What kind of influence on consumer behavior does this represent?
questions.explanation: A community spokesperson is a REFERENCE GROUP figure - someone consumers look to for opinions/credibility. Reference groups influence consumer behavior through aspiration or association.

questions.q: Which interpersonal influence is represented by a large group of people with a similar heritage?
questions.explanation: Shared heritage = CULTURE. Per the Lesson 34 table: 'Beliefs, values, and customs influence a consumer's spending.' Culture > Society in this framework.

questions.q: Which step of the complex decision-making process is involved after search?
questions.explanation: Consumer decision-making sequence: Need recognition → Search → EVALUATION → Buy → Post-purchase. After gathering info you compare alternatives = Evaluation.

questions.q: Which consumer behavioral factor uses the opinions of others to influence the decision-making process?
questions.explanation: Opinions of others = SOCIAL factor. This includes reference groups, family, friends, social media. Psychological = internal (motivation, perception, learning). Individual = personal traits.

questions.q: What aspect of marketing research would provide insight into buyer decision making?
questions.explanation: CONSUMER BEHAVIOR research is specifically about understanding HOW and WHY buyers make decisions. The other options are tactical implementations.

questions.q: A customer is making a purchase decision between several prepackaged meals by looking at nutrition information labeling to determine which has the least sodium. What type of problem-solving is being used?
questions.explanation: Comparing a few attributes among similar products = LIMITED problem-solving. Routine = no thought (habit). Extended = major decisions, deep research (cars/houses). Impulse = no thinking at all.

questions.q: A customer purchases fair trade branded chocolate because of the fair trade story on the packaging. What type of decision-making is being used?
questions.explanation: Buying based on ETHICAL credentials (fair trade, sustainable, organic, etc.) = ETHICAL CONSUMERISM. The other options are ethical philosophy frameworks, not consumer decision types.

questions.q: A realtor wants to sell luxury vacation homes and would like to identify potential buyers. What must the realtor understand to target this group?
choices: What the marketing budget is for selling luxury vacation homes
How buyers arrive at the decision to purchase a luxury vacation home
What the total costs are when selling luxury vacation homes
How the sales projections look next quarter
questions.explanation: To TARGET buyers, you must understand their DECISION-MAKING PROCESS. Budget/costs/projections are internal operations, not buyer understanding.

questions.q: Which of Maslow's hierarchy of needs includes the need to feel good about oneself and be respected by others?
questions.explanation: Maslow's pyramid (bottom to top): Physiological → Safety → Love/belonging → ESTEEM → Self-actualization. Esteem = self-respect AND respect from others. Love/belonging = relationships.

questions.q: Which group of people acts as a personal connection between a buyer and the company?
questions.explanation: SALESPEOPLE are the human face of the company - personal one-on-one connection with buyers. Marketers/advertisers/publicists communicate to broad audiences, not individual buyers.

questions.q: What is one factor a company should consider when designing a team selling approach?
choices: Who will lead the sales team
How to offer a complete package
When to communicate with the customer
questions.explanation: TEAM SELLING introduces the question of how multiple contributors share credit/commissions. Reward distribution is the unique challenge of team selling that doesn't exist in solo sales.

questions.q: An organization uses many touch points to reach customers with a variety of favorable messages about its product throughout the buying process. Which marketing concept is being illustrated?
questions.explanation: Many touch points + consistent favorable messages throughout buying process = INTEGRATED MARKETING COMMUNICATIONS (IMC). IMC coordinates all promotional channels for a unified message.

questions.q: Which activity is conducted by salespeople but not by marketers?
choices: Determine the consumer's risk tolerance for the purchase
questions.explanation: Risk tolerance is assessed in 1-on-1 conversation during the SALES PROCESS. Marketers handle copywriting/branding/4Ps at the strategic level. Salespeople handle individual buyer characteristics.

questions.q: Which step of the personal selling process involves interactions with potential customers?
questions.explanation: APPROACH = the FIRST contact/interaction with the prospect. Prospecting is identifying who to contact (no interaction yet). Presentation/objections come AFTER the approach establishes the interaction.

questions.q: Which types of points are blogs, wikis, and social media that companies use to build and sustain relationships with customers?
questions.explanation: TOUCH POINTS = any interaction between company and customer. Blogs/wikis/social are digital touch points. Building/sustaining relationships through interactions = touch points.

questions.q: A sales rep is told: 'Order the same quantity of the same product as last month, but change color from blue to red.' Which type of B2B buying situation is this?
questions.explanation: Same quantity + same product + ONE attribute change (color) = MODIFIED REBUY. Straight rebuy = identical re-order. New task = first-time purchase. Modified rebuy is the middle ground.

questions.q: A large hospital needs proprietary software for nursing staff. The IT department gives exact specifications. Senior management makes the final purchase decision based on IT's recommendation. Which role is the IT department playing?
questions.explanation: IT provides RECOMMENDATIONS that influence the decision but don't make it = INFLUENCER. Decider = senior management here. Gatekeeper = controls info flow. End user = the nurses who'd use the software.

questions.q: Which behavior by a salesperson can lead to ethical issues?
choices: Pricing products far above production costs
questions.explanation: Treating consumers as a COMMODITY (interchangeable, not as individuals) is dehumanizing and unethical. The other 3 are normal/ethical practices: relationships build trust, pricing reflects value, warnings ensure safety.

questions.q: Individual A and B are negotiating Individual A's pay package with multiple forms of pay and benefits. Their goals are not compatible, but they will have a long boss-worker relationship. Which approach to negotiation should they adopt?
questions.explanation: Long-term relationship + multiple variables = INTEGRATIVE (win-win) negotiation. Distributive = zero-sum. Inductive/deductive are reasoning approaches, not negotiation styles. Integrative = expand the pie.

questions.q: Two individuals share one administrative assistant between two departments. As sales grow, both need more support. They resolve it by emphasizing problem-solving and integration of each other's goals, creating a win-win. Which conflict-handling style was used?
questions.explanation: WIN-WIN + problem-solving + integrating both goals = COLLABORATION (high assertiveness + high cooperativeness). Avoidance = ignore. Accommodation = give in. Competition = win-lose. Collaboration is the only one yielding a win-win.

questions.q: What is the main function of marketing?
questions.explanation: Correct! The main function of marketing is to determine what customers value, want, or need, and then to position a product that meets that value.

questions.q: Which set of connections is created by marketers to generate value?
questions.explanation: Correct! Marketing generates value by determining what its target customers want or value, and then positioning a product to meet that need or desire.

questions.q: What is the relationship between sales and marketing in a firm's business strategy?
choices: Sales includes the process of communicating the value of a product or service, while marketing focuses on the actual exchange of money for a product or service.
Sales includes the exchange of money of a company's product or service, while marketing is the process of communicating the value of a product or service.
Sales includes the process of communicating the value of a product or service, while marketing involves calculating how much profit has been earned for a company within a fiscal year.
Sales includes calculating how much profit has been earned for a company within a fiscal year, while marketing is the process of communicating the value of a product or service.
questions.explanation: Correct! Sales includes the actual sale of the company's product, however marketing often works to help customers make their actual decision to purchase by communicating value.

questions.q: What is an example of a marketing activity?
choices: An executive reporting on stock performance
An engineer conducting quality control review
A manager conducting research on potential customers
questions.explanation: Correct! A marketing concept is defined as the use of marketing data to focus on the needs and wants of customers in order to develop marketing strategies that not only satisfy the needs of the customers, but also accomplish the goals of the organization

questions.q: Which element of the marketing mix is associated with social media advertising?
questions.explanation: Correct! Promotion refers to the ways in which is a product is advertised. Social media advertising is associated with the promotion element of the marketing mix.

questions.q: Which term is used when the price of a new product is lower than the competition with the goal of gaining market share?
questions.explanation: Correct! Price penetration is when a new product is priced lower than the perceived market price with the goal of increasing market share.

questions.q: In the marketing mix, what is meant by the term promotion?
choices: Goods, services, or ideas that a company offers to the market
Cost of a product, or what a company asks in exchange for a product
Getting the product from the producer to the customer
Communications between the company and the customer
questions.explanation: Correct! Promotion includes both the messages sent by the company and messages that customers send to the public about their experience.

questions.q: What is meant by the term "place" in the marketing mix?
questions.explanation: Correct! In the marketing mix, the term "place" refers to the distribution of the product. Place might be a traditional brick-and-mortar store, or it could be online.

questions.q: In the marketing mix, what is the meaning of the term “product”?
choices: Goods or services that meet customers' needs
questions.explanation: Correct! Products have unique set of features, design, name, and brand that are focused on target customers.

questions.q: What is the meaning of the term "uncontrollable elements"?
choices: Elements that are outside of a marketer's control
Elements in design and delivery of products
Elements that do not satisfy customers' needs and wants
questions.explanation: Correct! Uncontrollable elements are elements in the external marketing environment that cannot directly be controlled by marketers. Uncontrollable elements include things that are outside of the control of a company.

questions.q: A small tobacco shop that just opened wants to run advertising on a local radio station. When they approach the radio station’s sales department, they find that the station will not run their ad. What type of uncontrollable element prevents the running of this advertisement?
questions.explanation: Correct! The Federal Trade Commission prohibits the advertising of tobacco products on radio and television.

questions.q: A manufacturer of children's toys discovers that a number of products that it makes and sells have been duplicated and are selling alongside their products on various e-commerce sites. The duplicate products appear to be made overseas and are selling for 30% lower. The company's sales department feels pressure to lower pricing to match that of the duplicate products in an effort not to lose sales. Which element in the marketing environment is demonstrated in this situation?
questions.explanation: Correct! Duplicate products at a lower price reflect a change in the competition that the company needs to address.

questions.q: A restaurant owner has noticed a shift in the restaurant's customer attitudes towards locally-sourced and sustainable ingredients and is changing the menu in an effort to cater to these customers. What element of the marketing environment does this represent?
questions.explanation: Correct! The restaurant owner's move from a national supplier to locally-sourced ingredients reflecting customer values is an example of socio-cultural factors.

questions.q: A large general contractor is having trouble meeting its labor needs, given the low unemployment in the area. The company begins advertising for construction workers in an adjacent state, offering a generous sign-on bonus in an effort to fill open positions. What element of the marketing environment is the company addressing?
questions.explanation: Correct! Economic variables, such as low unemployment, affects how a company markets its products and services.

questions.q: A small startup company plans to sell affordable footwear, manufactured from sustainable materials. Company leadership assembles an ethics panel to ensure their products meet their goals of sustainability and eco-friendliness, while finding a niche market in the marketplace. The members of the ethics panel determine if their products are affordable and can be realistically marketed to certain market segments. Which ethics consideration is this company addressing?
questions.explanation: Correct! The ethics of price consideration involves pricing products at a point that is fair in the market, does not discriminate between different buyers of the same product, does not collude with competitors to fix prices, and does not set prices below market to drive competitors out of the market.

questions.q: A small startup company plans to sell affordable footwear, manufactured from sustainable materials. Company leadership assembles an ethics panel to ensure their products meet their goals of sustainability and eco-friendliness, while finding a niche market in the marketplace. The members of the ethics panel take into consideration the labor conditions under which the materials are grown, harvested, and shipped to market. Which ethics consideration is this company addressing?
questions.explanation: Correct! The ethics of product consideration involves the determination of whether or not the product is environmentally friendly, if it provides value and meets the needs of the customers, and if the product is in the best interest of customers in society.

questions.q: A small startup company plans to sell affordable footwear manufactured from sustainable materials and has assembled an ethics panel to ensure the products meet this goal. The panel takes into consideration the labor conditions of the distribution channel and if the product can be purchased at the price promised. The ethics panel also wants to know whether the workers in the company can actually afford to purchase the item themselves. Which ethics consideration is being reviewed by this company?
questions.explanation: Correct! The ethical consideration of place is concerned with the distribution channel and whether it can deliver the product at the price and quality promised, labor conditions for the distribution channel are fair and humane, companies in the distribution channel have similar ethical considerations, and the privacy of customers is protected.

questions.q: A small startup company plans to sell affordable footwear, manufactured from sustainable materials. Company leadership has assembled an ethics panel to ensure that the products meet this goal, while finding a niche market in the marketplace. The panel is also considering the marketing claims for the products to determine if the benefits and intrinsic value promised are realistic. Which ethics consideration is this company addressing?
questions.explanation: Correct! The ethics of product promotion considers whether or not the product delivers the benefits advertised, delivers the value promised of the customer, and whether or not the product is being marketed to the appropriate audience.

questions.q: A marketing department develops a marketing plan that focuses on departmental goals and the actions the department must take to achieve them. Which component provides this detailed information?
questions.explanation: Correct! The plan includes the marketing department's goals and then the objectives, actions, efforts, and other details needed to meet those goals.

questions.q: A business team is revising the document meant to guide the marketing department, managers, and teams as they work to identify the department's objectives and how to reach them. Which document is being revised?
questions.explanation: Correct! The marketing plan includes the marketing department's goals, and then the objectives, actions, efforts, and other details needed to meet those goals. It is the guiding document requested in the scenario.

questions.q: During a meeting, a marketing department describes the sales goals for the year, the target markets selected, and the actions the department will undertake to reach these goals. Which portion of the marketing planning process was discussed during this meeting?
questions.explanation: Correct! This meeting focused on the marketing strategy. This strategy determines how a marketing mix (product, price, place, and promotion) should be used to achieve the marketing objectives.

questions.q: A marketing manager reviews monthly sales reports, sales forecasts for the upcoming quarter, budgets for advertising campaigns, and product reviews from customers and compares this data against the marketing objectives described in the marketing plan. Which step in the marketing planning process is being reviewed by this manager?
questions.explanation: Correct! Monitoring and control is the last step in this process and would involve these tasks.

questions.q: A marketing department is reviewing a recent SWOT analysis and notes entries for economic and social trends. What kind of forces are being reviewed during this process?
questions.explanation: Correct! The forces listed are external to the organization. They may be influenced but are not fully under the organization's control.

questions.q: A sales manager is reviewing the current products in the company's portfolio and sees that one product that has been sold for a decade is now the slowest-selling product in a mature industry. Which Boston Consulting Group (BCG) model category could be used for this product?
questions.explanation: Correct! This product is a dog that is exhausted. It is a product with a low market share in a mature industry, the definition of a "dog" item. There is no room for growth, so there is no reason for further investment.

questions.q: A sales manager reviews the current products in the company's portfolio and sees that one product the company began selling for about a year is now showing high market share in a fast-growing industry. Which Boston Consulting Group (BCG) model category could be used for this product?
questions.explanation: Correct! This product is likely a star selling with a high market share in a fast-growing market, which is the definition of a star.

questions.q: A manufacturer produces a Bluetooth thermometer for grilling. The product is high-end and priced accordingly. A year after introduction to the market, one of the company's salespeople sees another company's ad for a very similar Bluetooth thermometer at a much lower price. Which of Porter's Five Forces is occurring in relation to this product?
questions.explanation: Correct! The newly-advertised thermometer represents competitive rivalry because a competitor has created a very similar Bluetooth thermometer at a much lower price point.

questions.q: A firm is planning to launch a new product. They also have adopted a vision for how they will achieve their objectives. What type of planning is being used by this firm?
questions.explanation: Correct! A marketing strategy is a vision for how you will achieve the specified objectives in the marketing plan. This firm has developed a vision for how they will achieve the objectives.

questions.q: A firm is launching a new product and has developed a plan outlining specific activities and allocation of resources needed to implement that plan over a given period of time. What type of planning is being used by this firm?
questions.explanation: Correct! Tactical plans specify the activities and allocation of resources (people, equipment, and money) needed to implement the strategic plan over a given period, which is what the firm in this example has developed.

questions.q: A company's leadership decides to increase product sales by signing an agreement with a celebrity to execute an influencer social media campaign. What type of planning is being used by this company?
questions.explanation: Correct! Tactical planning defines specific activities to reach a goal. In this scenario, the company leadership has identified that its goal is to increase product sales and has chosen to achieve this through tactical implementation of an influencer social media campaign.

questions.q: A firm has determined that they want to use social media influencers and search engine–paid ads to meet a sales objective. What type of planning is being used by this firm?
questions.explanation: Correct! Tactical planning includes the actions a company implements to affect the controllable elements of the strategy; the tactics in this example are to use social media influencers and search engine–paid ads.

questions.q: A sales manager uses market research to examine a geographic area the company wants to consider for expansion. What is a benefit of this market research?
questions.explanation: Correct! One benefit of marketing research is determining potential customers. Marketing research can be used to determine the population most likely to use the product.

questions.q: Which type of research yields data that are useful to a sales manager who wishes to better understand the company's customers?
questions.explanation: Correct! Marketing research would provide a profile of the company's customers. "The purpose of marketing research is to help companies make better business decisions and gain advantages against the competition by better understanding their current and target customers."

questions.q: A sales manager reviews the latest reports for a primary product in a rapidly growing market and sees that sales have dropped significantly. The manager conducts marketing research to understand the drop in sales. Which benefit of marketing research will assist this sales manager?
questions.explanation: Correct! One of the questions marketing research can answer is, "Who are competitors in the market?"

questions.q: A company is introducing a new product and wants to conduct market research to position the item for maximum growth and sales. Which component of marketing research provides this information?
questions.explanation: Correct! Product research will meet this need and is already part of the research and development process.

questions.q: A sales manager is analyzing the sales reports for the prior year in an effort to budget for the next year's marketing. What type of data is this manager reviewing?
questions.explanation: Correct! Sales numbers represent quantitative, numerical data that can be used to budget for next year's marketing. The data are secondary because the sales department generated the data without the marketing manager's input.

questions.q: A marketing manager wants to better understand customer wants and needs in a product. The marketing department sends out an open ended question survey with a 10% off coupon to current customers to ask about their product preferences. Which kind of research is this survey?
questions.explanation: Correct! This kind of open-ended survey is an example of qualitative research. "Qualitative research explores ideas, perceptions, and behaviors in depth with a relatively small number of research participants."

questions.q: The marketing department hires a research company to conduct surveys with retail owners to evaluate its new product distributed to retailers. Which type of data collection is used in this example?
questions.explanation: Correct! Primary research is designed to address a specific company inquiry or problem and is conducted directly with the individuals for whom the inquiry is designed. In this case, the marketing department is hiring a research company to conduct surveys directly with the market, which represents primary research.

questions.q: Which data set is considered secondary research?
questions.explanation: Correct! A company's customer list is a set of data already assembled by the company.

questions.q: A CEO needs solutions to specific problems in the company and contracts with a consulting company to conduct primary research and provide recommendations. What is a benefit of this type of research to the CEO?
choices: Uses data that are already available
questions.explanation: Correct! Primary data may directly address the needs and concerns of the researcher. "Primary data directly address the problems or challenges of interest to you."

questions.q: The owner of a small business wants to invest in expansion and needs demographic data on customers in the area, but has a small budget for this kind of information. Which kind of research will fit this owner's needs?
questions.explanation: Correct! Secondary research is more cost-effective than primary research and applies to a larger group or situation. "Secondary data are more cost-effective and may even be freely available."

questions.q: A sales manager needs information on potential customers that fit both a specific demographic and live in a specific geographic location. A salesperson suggests using secondary research, but the manager decides to use primary research instead. Why did the manager choose primary research over secondary research for this purpose?
choices: Primary research is cheaper to conduct.
questions.explanation: Correct! Primary research is customized to the organization's need so the demographic and location targets can be easily incorporated into the process. This will provide the information the manager needs.

questions.q: Which type of research consists of source data previously collected for other purposes?
questions.explanation: Correct! Secondary data are just the data collected for some other reason or purpose. These data have been "previously collected for other purposes."

questions.q: A sales manager for a small company has no budget for research but needs data to expand a marketing campaign. The manager hopes to increase the rate of repeat purchases from current customers. Which form of data meets this sales manager's needs?
questions.explanation: Correct! Internal data are something the sales manager already has access to, so there is no cost. A company’s internal data, such as sales and marketing records, customer account information, product purchasing, and usage data, are typical secondary data sources and can provide the information on customers needed by this manager.

questions.q: A marketing manager plans to expand a current marketing campaign to reach a well-documented market segment that the company does not currently attract. Which data source should the manager use to meet this goal?
questions.explanation: Correct! Syndicated market research would have this kind of data. "Syndicated research of consumer data for purchase as well as database information on consumer purchases and behavior" would help expand the manager's campaign.

questions.q: What is one ethical consideration marketers should follow when collecting primary data?
choices: Ask for consent to gather the data from surveys.
Be transparent about how data gathered from company reports will be applied.
Require customer questionnaires to be completed before submission.
Avoid stereotypes when searching the internet.
questions.explanation: Correct! An ethical consideration marketers should use includes receiving consent to collect data.

questions.q: Which ethical practice should be used to enrich the information obtained from focus groups?
questions.explanation: Correct! Organizations should ask clear questions of their focus groups to obtain the best information.

questions.q: A group of marketers is collecting their own data for an organization's business project. They will be storing the records in a shared file that all organizational employees can access. Which ethical issue should these researchers be concerned with in regard to these data?
questions.explanation: Correct! Security will ensure that personal data will not be compromised by internal marketing researchers and employees. This will also ensure that a public data breach will not occur.

questions.q: All of a company's employees were required to complete a survey. Which ethical consideration has the company violated?
questions.explanation: Correct! Because the company is requiring employees to submit, employees are compelled to respond and have no choice or consent.

questions.q: What is a company's market share?
choices: A company's presence in a trade show offering
A company's total advertising budget on a specific medium
A company's public image rating relating to environmental issues
A company’s percentage of the total sales in an industry
questions.explanation: Correct! Market share is a company’s percentage of the total sales in a particular market. The total sales can be measured in units sold, or total revenue can measure marketing share.

questions.q: What does the strategic opportunity matrix examine?
questions.explanation: Correct! The strategic opportunity matrix helps companies focus on different growth strategies for markets and products by examining new versus existing markets and new versus existing products.

questions.q: What is the name of a means of evaluating a company's plans for growth based on new versus existing markets and new versus existing products?
questions.explanation: Correct! The strategic opportunity matrix organizes growth strategies in a framework based on new versus existing markets and new versus existing products.

questions.q: Why is a growth strategy important to a company?
choices: It allows a company to determine how many new employees that the company needs to hire.
It ensures a company has made best efforts to ensure that employees' retirement accounts increase in value.
It provides a planning tool for employees to further their career by utilizing internal growth and development programs.
It provides a planning tool to simplify, organize, and focus the possible options for growth for the company.
questions.explanation: Correct! The strategic opportunity matrix is a tool to develop a growth strategy. It helps a company determine the actions required for growth.

questions.q: Which growth strategy utilizes new markets with existing products using the strategic opportunity matrix?
questions.explanation: Correct! A market development strategy relates to new markets with existing products.

questions.q: Which growth strategy utilizes new markets with new products using the strategic opportunity matrix?
questions.explanation: Correct! A diversification strategy relates to new products in new markets.

questions.q: Which growth strategy utilizes existing markets with existing products using the strategic opportunity matrix?
questions.explanation: Correct! A market penetration strategy relates to existing products in existing markets.

questions.q: Which growth strategy utilizes existing markets with new products using the strategic opportunity matrix?
questions.explanation: Correct! A product development strategy relates to new products in existing markets.

questions.q: What is diversification?
choices: Diversification increases profitability through greater sales volume obtained from new products and new markets.
Diversification ensures that as more employees are hired, equal opportunity hiring practices are followed.
Diversification decreases the number of investments a company has in order to vary its portfolio.
Diversification ensures that other brands are not confused with the company's brand.
questions.explanation: Correct! Diversification seeks to increase profitability through greater sales volume obtained from new products and new markets.

questions.q: In which stage of the product life cycle does new product development occur?
questions.explanation: Correct! Companies typically see new product development as the first stage in the overall strategic process of product life cycle management used to maintain or grow market share. This stage is the product introduction stage.

questions.q: What does a market development strategy do for a company?
choices: Delivers marketing materials to customers via emails, online ads, and other media outlets
Focuses on retaining current customers using new incentives and market research
Targets new customers and new segments to expand the sales base
Designs new point-of-sale experience and online storefront to give a fresh image for a company
questions.explanation: Correct! A market development strategy seeks to expand the market by finding new customers.

questions.q: When does market penetration occur?
choices: When a company increases production of a product to meet increased demand
When a company increases sales in a market in which its products already exist
When a company improves its previous product in a current market
When a company removes a line of products to exit a current market
questions.explanation: Correct! Market penetration occurs when a company infiltrates a market in which current products already exist. The best way to achieve this is by gaining the customers of competitors. Other ways include attracting non-users of your product or convincing current clients to use more of your product.

questions.q: What is customer relationship management (CRM)?
choices: Conducting data analysis about how to better meet the needs of the company
Working with software designed to capture external data about customers
Providing public users with access to company data to inform selling opportunities
Using processes implemented by a company that enhance customer interaction
questions.explanation: Correct! CRM is a combination of policies, processes, and strategies implemented by a company that unify its customer interaction and provide a mechanism for tracking customer information.

questions.q: What is the purpose of customer relationship management (CRM) software?
choices: Serving several essential functions for customers and human resources
Delivering a marketing mix tailored to the needs and interests of sales personnel
Supporting processes by storing information about customers
Helping sales and marketing organize data about employees
questions.explanation: Correct! CRM software is used to support these processes, storing information on current, past, and prospective customers

questions.q: Which system should be used for a business to develop a customized cosmetics tutorial guide for an individual woman based on the previous feedback?
questions.explanation: Correct! Customer relationship management (CRM) is based on meeting the needs of the customer. CRM software is used to support these processes, storing information on current, past, and prospective customers.

questions.q: How does a customer relationship management (CRM) system improve services to the customer?
choices: Allows for secure online chats between sales and customers
Provides a social media platform for the organization
Provides information for targeted marketing and sales purposes
Allows customers to pay their bills online using an easy interface
questions.explanation: Correct! A CRM allows an organization to manage customer data and provide information for a targeted marketing and sales purposes.

questions.q: How does a customer relationship management (CRM) system benefit a customer?
choices: Creates avenues for customers to contact vendors on the supply chain
Individualizes marketing and sales messages to customers
Allows customers to manage the various contacts of the organization
Provides sophisticated analytics to allow customers to manage their data
questions.explanation: Correct! A CRM allows an organization to customize the marketing and sales messages that a customer is given. This information is given by the customer, based on the data collected from their experience.

questions.q: A clothing store uses a customer relationship management (CRM) system and notices that when one line of the clothing is purchased, customer retention is low. What is a benefit of CRM for this store?
choices: Sales campaigns can be created by working with sales personnel.
More coupons can be mailed to customers.
Advertisements can be sent to new areas of town.
Customer satisfaction can be improved by tracking buyer behavior.
questions.explanation: Correct! By identifying the customer's that are not being retained by the company, it can work on the supply chain with their vendor to help improve customer satisfaction.

questions.q: A manager gives feedback to a team that their core customers were very satisfied. Which benefit to customer relationship management (CRM) is being used by this manager?
questions.explanation: Correct! Analytical benefits use data to understand who the company’s core customers are, how they behave, what they are looking for, and how satisfied they are.

questions.q: Which is a benefit that a customer relationship management (CRM) can provide a company?
choices: Analyzing why a potential customer did not make a purchase
Analyzing total sales per sales personnel
Providing external data to analyze a marketing problem
Providing data to the company across the customer life cycle
questions.explanation: Correct! A CRM is designed to help an organization follow a customer from beginning of the sales process to the end.

questions.q: A beverage company purchases advertising to introduce a new line of energy drinks. Which stage of the customer life cycle does this action illustrate?
questions.explanation: Correct! Reach is the stage of the customer life cycle in which the seller is endeavoring to attract the attention of a prospective customer.

questions.q: A salesperson for a medical equipment company provides marketing materials for the practice manager at a doctor's office. After three months, the practice manager orders three products. Which stage of the customer life cycle does this series of actions illustrate?
questions.explanation: Correct! After reaching the perspective customer and bringing the prospect into the sphere of influence, the prospect is converted into a paying customer. Conversion is the stage of the customer life cycle where the seller turns the prospect into a paying customer.

questions.q: A company sends an email to its customers with a 20% off coupon, if they make a purchase within the next 48 hours. Which stage of the customer life cycle does this action illustrate?
questions.explanation: Correct! The company is sending emails to existing customers. This is an example of retention. Retention is the stage of the customer life cycle where a seller engages with current customers in an effort to maintain them as customers going forward.

questions.q: An individual clicks on a link to request more information about a product. A salesperson emails the prospect information and pricing and then offers to call with more information. Which stage of the customer life cycle does this series of actions illustrate?
questions.explanation: Correct! This is the point in the customer life cycle where the seller is endeavoring to bring the prospect closer to the conversion stage. Acquisition is the stage of the customer lifecycle where the seller is endeavoring to pull the prospective customer into their sphere of influence.

questions.q: A sales manager is reviewing sales reports from the previous quarter and wants to increase sales in the upcoming quarter by focusing on existing customers with a high customer lifetime value. What is one way to maintain an ongoing relationship with these customers?
questions.explanation: Correct! Marketing is an effective way to cultivate and maintain an ongoing relationship with high-value customers.

questions.q: What should a sales manager use to determine customer lifetime value?
choices: Average number of contacts with the customer
Total profit from all customer purchases
Average number of touchpoints reaching the customer
questions.explanation: Correct! The total profit margin per average sale is one of the important factors to consider when determining a customer's lifetime value.

questions.q: What is considered a less tangible benefit of customer lifetime value?
questions.explanation: Correct! Long-term customers are more likely to be loyal to the brand and ambassadors for the company. This loyalty may provide valuable feedback to marketing.

questions.q: What is a benefit of knowing a customer's lifetime value?
questions.explanation: Correct! Customer lifetime value is one measure that marketing may use to determine the profitability and effectiveness of marketing campaigns.

questions.q: What does customer equity measure?
choices: Value of the product or service provided by the company
Customer assessment of the value of the brand
Tendency to remain with a brand regardless of value
questions.explanation: Correct! Customer equity refers to the total combined customer lifetime values for all the purchases the customers make for that product over their total buying experience.

questions.q: What is a driver for customer equity?
questions.explanation: Correct! The three main drivers of customer equity are brand, retention, and value equity.

questions.q: A person has a computer using Platform A. When it comes time to replace the computer, the Platform A computer costs $1,000, while a comparable Platform B computer costs $500. The person chooses to purchase the Platform A computer despite the difference in cost. Which driver to customer equity does this individual's decision represent?
questions.explanation: Correct! Retention equity explains the tendency of the customer to stick with the brand even when it is priced higher than an otherwise equal product.

questions.q: A customer is choosing either Company A or Company B chocolate chip cookies. Ultimately, the customer chooses the Company A cookies because of his or her preference for that manufacturer's type of product. Which driver of customer equity does this individual's decision represent?
questions.explanation: Correct! Brand equity is how the customer assesses the value of the brand over its objective value.

questions.q: How is customer satisfaction defined?
choices: The lifetime value of a customer minus the cost of obtaining and retaining that customer
The number of customers who refer their friends to a firm
The number of promoters of a brand minus the number of detractors
The feeling a customer experiences when an offering meets or exceeds expectations
questions.explanation: Correct! Customer satisfaction is all about meeting or exceeding the customer's expectations.

questions.q: What is a key factor of customer satisfaction?
questions.explanation: Correct! In researching satisfaction, firms generally ask customers whether their product or service has met or exceeded expectations. Thus, expectations are a key factor behind satisfaction.

questions.q: A customer has contacted a company for buying a car and is asking questions about gas mileage and performance. The company's representative is careful to provide appropriate prepurchase information to the potential customer. Which piece of information should be transferred to a customer at this stage of communication?
questions.explanation: Correct! Setting the customer's expectations at or slightly lower than the expected experience will create customer satisfaction.

questions.q: A store has a policy that all customer-facing employees can give away one $5 flower bouquet a day to customers who they feel need a bright spot in their day. Which aspect of customer satisfaction is being demonstrated by this store policy?
questions.explanation: Correct! Empowering employees to drop what they are doing to do something special for a customer can certainly delight customers and is the type of action illustrated in the scenario.

questions.q: What is contained in a nondisclosure agreement (NDA)?
choices: The information that is proprietary and how the seller can use that information
The list of customers that cannot be contacted and the penalties for violation
The type of customer information that can be sold
The pricing agreement between vendors and buyers
questions.explanation: Correct! An NDA is common in situations between vendors and business buyers.

questions.q: Which U.S. federal act establishes standards for commercial email?
choices: Federal Administrative Information and Protection Regulation (FAI-APR)
Controlling the Assault of Non-Solicited Pornography and Marketing (CAN-SPAM)
questions.explanation: Correct! This act was passed in 2003 and gives consumers the ability to opt out of communications.

questions.q: Which action accurately reflects when permission marketing should be used by a manager?
choices: When offering marketing messages to buyers
Before creating a campaign for a boss
Before asking about a buyer's experience
questions.explanation: Correct! Permission marketing suggests that if customers give permission, they are open to receive the message. It is used during this type of customer interaction.

questions.q: A business sells products, services, or raw materials to other businesses. What type of transactions is the focus of this business?
questions.explanation: Correct! B2B stands for business-to-business transactions . B2B transactions are sales to another company that consumes the product or services as part of operating the business or uses the product in the assembly of the final product it sells to consumers.

questions.q: A company focuses on B2B transactions. Who is the customer for this type of business?
choices: The CTO for a company looking for a vacation package for their family
A college student buying their books for school
The CEO of a name brand company buying a new personal cellphone
A college buying laptops for an incoming freshman class
questions.explanation: Correct! A college buying laptops for their students is one business (or other type of entity) that is purchasing products from another business. B2B stands for "business-to-business" and involves sales to another company that consumes the product or services as part of operating the business or uses the product in the assembly of the final product sold to consumers.

questions.q: A business manufactures cell phones and smart watches for end users. What type of transaction is the focus of this business?
questions.explanation: Correct! B2C stands for "business-to-consumer" and relates to sales directly to the individuals who consume a finished product for personal use (also called end users).

questions.q: Which example illustrates a market segment?
questions.explanation: Correct! This is a segment of possible consumers that marketing efforts might be directed towards.

questions.q: Which example aligns with the purpose of market segmentation?
choices: Branding to align with all customer needs
Launching a design for a specific customer group
Promoting a product using mass marketing
Creating one ad for all products on social media
questions.explanation: Correct! Market segmentation occurs when a company divides its overall customer base into segments, or groups, based on unifying characteristics. This response identifies a specific customer group, which indicates the use of market segmentation.

questions.q: Why would a company want to focus on specific segments of a market?
choices: To study buyer behaviors to determine the next demographic so the company's product or service will be marketed correctly
To stagger the production process so bulk jobs can be handled in batches of similar work
To focus on a specific demographic or interest group so marketing efforts are reaching the intended audience
To pay back segments of a loan incrementally so the company can reduce their interest burden
questions.explanation: Correct! Most companies cannot target the entire market. By focusing on a specific segment, the product or service can be more strategically positioned to market to the segment.

questions.q: What is the term used to describe the practice of identifying customers who might be interested in a company's products or services?
questions.explanation: Correct! Segmentation is the process of dividing the market into subgroups of consumers.

questions.q: A company has decided to target customers who are actively engaged in fitness. What type of segmentation variable is the company using?
questions.explanation: Correct! Lifestyle, personality, interests, values, attitudes, and opinions all fall under the psychographic segmentation strategy. In this scenario, the company is targeting customers based on their fitness lifestyles, which represents psychographic segmentation.

questions.q: Which criteria is part of a psychographic segmentation strategy?
questions.explanation: Correct! Lifestyle, personality, interests, values, attitudes, and opinions are all a part of the psychographic segmentation strategy.

questions.q: What criteria is examined to create a product-related segmentation?
questions.explanation: Correct! Benefits provided by the good or service offered, usage rates, or brand loyalty are all part of the product-related segmentation strategy.

questions.q: A retail manager determines that the majority of store purchases come from university students and decides to increase promotions to that group. What is the purpose of this strategy?
questions.explanation: Correct! Identifying a market helps a company focus its marketing efforts on those who are most likely to buy its products or services. Concentrating on potential customers lets the firm use its resources efficiently. This retailer is targeting buyers interested in fast-fashion apparel to advertise only where customers will access social information. This will create an efficient use of resources for the retailer by advertising to produce the best return on investment.

questions.q: A marketing manager is determining the customers who would be most inclined to purchase a new product. Why is the manager performing this activity?
questions.explanation: Correct! Identifying a target market helps a company focus its marketing efforts on those who are most likely to buy its products or services. Concentrating on potential customers lets the firm use its resources efficiently.

questions.q: A company lacks the resources to market every brand in its portfolio to every market segment. Which strategy maximizes the use of these limited marketing resources?
questions.explanation: Correct! Target marketing helps companies focus its marketing efforts on those who are most likely to purchase its products or services.

questions.q: A company is preparing to launch a new product accessory for their mobile devices. The business manager reviews sales reports of the mobile devices to determine which specific customer groups would be most interested in this new accessory. What is a benefit of the manager's approach?
choices: Indicates which customers are more likely to buy
Identifies identical products in the marketplace
Improves forecasting of all company products
questions.explanation: Correct! Market segmentation will indicate which customers should be targeted.

questions.q: Why is differentiated marketing considered expensive?
choices: It focuses on mass marketing for commodity items.
It requires the development of unique products to fit each target segment.
It focuses on marketing techniques that sell luxury goods during a recession.
It requires that marketers get to know a small geographic area.
questions.explanation: Correct! Each unique product and market segment requires its own marketing plans and execution: unique messages, campaigns, and promotional tactics and investments.

questions.q: A luxury watch designer markets exclusively to professional golfers. What type of targeting strategy is utilized by this company?
questions.explanation: Correct! Concentrated marketing is niche marketing. An organization that adopts a concentrated marketing strategy gains an advantage by focusing all efforts on only one or a small handful of segments. This watch designer markets exclusively to professional golfers, which is a concentrated strategy.

questions.q: Which targeting strategy caters to a small segment of a neighborhood?
questions.explanation: Correct! Micromarketing can be very powerful by giving consumers exactly what they want, when they want it. However, to achieve large-scale success with this approach, companies must figure out how to meet highly individualized needs efficiently and profitably.

questions.q: Which targeting strategy is synonymous with mass marketing?
questions.explanation: Correct! Undifferentiated marketing, also called mass marketing, involves marketing to the entire market the same way.

questions.q: What is the purpose of product positioning?
choices: To identify the specific group of customers towards which a firm should direct its marketing efforts
To determine the place an offering should occupy in a given market, relative to other customer alternatives
To articulate the competitive advantages of a company's products
To select potential customers who may be interested in the company's products
questions.explanation: Correct! Positioning is a strategic process that marketers use to determine the place an offering should occupy in a given market, relative to other customer alternatives.

questions.q: A company positions its running shoes to convince customers that they will run faster, be stronger, and be influencers of athletic fashion when wearing these shoes. What is the purpose of this product's positioning?
questions.explanation: Correct! When a company positions by attitude, a product is being marketed in such a way that customers will consider the product and benefits as important to their lives and influence. This company is marketing its running shoes to create customer attitudes about running faster, being stronger, and influencing others for athletic fashion.

questions.q: Why is positioning essential when launching a new offering?
choices: It helps the customer understand how the offering fits into the available choices.
It ensures that marketers understand how much to spend on the product launch.
It helps the customer understand why the company created the new offering.
It ensures that marketers understand and define a target market.
questions.explanation: Correct! Positioning helps marketers and customers understand how the offering fits into the set of available choices and makes a set of claims about why customers should consider it.

questions.q: An athletic shoe company promotes its new high-performance running shoes by sponsoring a U.S. Olympic athlete. The company wants potential customers to identify with the athlete and see an association between the shoes and the athlete’s performance. What is this strategy an example of?
questions.explanation: Correct! The customers will see the athlete performing at a high level and associate the running shoes with the athlete's competitive advantage. This is an example of product positioning, which is the process of creating an image of the product in the customers' minds.

questions.q: A company markets its product as the best value in its category. Which positioning strategy is being used by this company?
questions.explanation: Correct! The price positioning strategy positions the product as the lowest cost or best value.

questions.q: A company is marketing a tablet based on its capabilities to be used as both an e-reader and a browsing device. Which positioning strategy is being used by this company?
questions.explanation: Correct! Product attribute positioning is based on a characteristic that defines a product and will influence the customer’s decision to purchase. In this case, the product attributes being focused on are its multiple use cases.

questions.q: A supermarket is consistently rated at the top in customer service among all shopping categories in a nationwide survey. Because of this rating, the supermarket frequently outperforms other stores in its market. Which concept is illustrated by this supermarket's status?
questions.explanation: Correct! A competitive advantage is some trait, quality, or capability that allows you to outperform the competition. In this example, the supermarket's consistent top customer service rating is its competitive advantage.

questions.q: Which statement accurately describes the purpose of positioning maps?
choices: Creates a picture of how competitors are positioned in the market
Tracks company sales performance quarter over quarter
Creates a budget strategy to promote a new product
Tracks the preferred marketing tactics used to promote a new product
questions.explanation: Correct! Positioning maps identify two pieces of key criteria that customers use when deciding what to buy and set these as the horizontal and vertical axes. Then competitors are placed in the space where they seem to fit.

questions.q: A marketing manager wants to better understand how the company's customers choose products. Which component is this manager trying to understand?
questions.explanation: Correct! This marketing manager is trying to understand consumer behavior when considering how customers choose the company's product. "Consumer behavior, in its broadest sense, is concerned with understanding both how purchase decisions are made and how products or services are consumed or experienced."

questions.q: A sales manager wants to know which internal and external forces affect what a consumer will purchase. What kind of information is needed by this manager?
questions.explanation: Correct! Marketing research would give this manager the necessary information. "Through marketing research, marketers seek to understand what impacts consumer behavior."

questions.q: A marketing manager requests data on the company's consumer buying patterns. How will this data assist the manager?
choices: By shaping the company's research and development
By showing return on investment for marketing campaigns
By shaping the company's market offerings
By showing how many salespeople the company needs
questions.explanation: Correct! Consumer behavior data assist in marketing efforts. A market offering is shaped by consumer behavior data.

questions.q: A marketing manager commissions consumer behavior research on the company's customers. What will this research indicate to this manager?
choices: The average profit per item sold to each customer
How effective the marketing plan was
How products or services are consumed
The average age of the company's customer
questions.explanation: Correct! Consumer research indicates how products or services are chosen and consumed.

questions.q: A consumer is ready to purchase a new car. Safety, reliability, and cost are the primary needs for this purchase.
